questions.question: How was the training set filtered to reduce homologous leakage from the 100-protein validation set?

options.A: HHblits HMM hits with e-value below 0.1 against validation proteins were removed, leaving 34,691 train and 88 validation proteins after length filtering
options.B: All proteins with sequence identity above 50% were retained, leaving 50,914 training proteins
options.C: The validation set was chosen randomly after training and contained 669 proteins
options.D: Only proteins shorter than 100 residues were kept, with no homology filtering

questions.rationale: The authors use HMM-based screening and later remove sequences longer than 500 residues.
questions.evidence_quote: To efficiently validate models during training and minimize possible over-fitting, we separated 100 proteins from the ProteinNet set and compared their Hidden Markov Models generated by HHblits with the Hidden Markov Models of other proteins in the training dataset and validation set using HHblits. Any proteins, which had hits with these 100 validation proteins at an e-value cut-off of less than 0.1, were removed. This left us with the final 39120 proteins for the training set. After removing any proteins with a length more than 500 from both the training and validation sets, the final training and validation sets have 34691 and 88 proteins, respectively.

questions.question: What distinguishes the two independent test sets used for homolog-poor and de novo-like evaluation?

options.A: SPOT-2018 contains 669 post-2018 proteins, while Neff1-2018 isolates 46 with Neff=1; CASP14-FM adds 15 free-modeling targets
options.B: SPOT-2018 contains 46 proteins and CASP14-FM contains 669 homolog-rich targets
options.C: Neff1-2018 contains 15 proteins with known templates, while CASP14-FM contains 100 validation proteins
options.D: All sets were sampled from the training proteins before 2016

questions.rationale: The benchmark design includes both post-training structures with stringent HMM filtering and subsets specifically lacking homologs or templates.
questions.evidence_quote:
This led to 669 proteins as a stringent test set named SPOT-2018.
To test how predictors perform on de-novo proteins and proteins without homologs, we separated 46 proteins from SPOT-2018 which have Neff=1 forming a test set called Neff1-2018.

questions.question: Which ESM-1b attention features entered the six-model ensemble?

options.A: Symmetrized, APC-corrected maps from all 20 heads in the last layer or from 20 heads in every layer
options.B: Only the ESM-1b final embedding vector, without attention maps
options.C: All 34 transformer layers' raw unsymmetrized attention probabilities
options.D: One attention head from the first layer after sequence-profile concatenation

questions.rationale: The feature design compares the last layer against all layers, using twenty heads and applying symmetrization plus APC.
questions.evidence_quote: Attention maps from ESM-1b were gathered by using all twenty attention heads from the last layer of the transformer as well as twenty attention heads from every layer of the ESM-1b model. For both cases, we symmetrized and applied average product corrections (APC) to the extracted attention maps

questions.question: How did the contact definition and sequence-separation categories used for evaluation differ?

options.A: A contact was Cβ–Cβ distance ≤8 Å; long, medium, and short pairs were separated by ≥24, 12–23, and 7–11 residues
options.B: A contact was Cα distance <4 Å; long, medium, and short were ≥12, 8–11, and 1–7 residues
options.C: A contact was any atom within 8 Å; classes were based on spatial rather than sequence distance
options.D: A contact was Cβ distance ≤10 Å; pairs at least 7 residues apart were all long-range

questions.rationale: The evaluation follows the stated CASP distance threshold and bins residue pairs by sequence separation.
questions.evidence_quote: protein residues are considered to be in contact when there is an inter-residue distance of ≤ 8.0 Å between two C β atoms. A contact between two residues is classified into three types: long (at least 24 residues apart), medium (between 12 to 23 residues apart) and short (between 7-11 residues apart) ranges.

questions.question: What network depth and feature combinations defined the final model family?

options.A: Six ResNet12 models with 64 channels and 3×3 kernels combined last/all-layer ESM attention with optional one-hot and SPOT-1D-Single features
options.B: A single 30-block ResNet used only one-hot inputs and no ESM attention
options.C: Six Transformer-34 models used only MSA profiles and 128 channels
options.D: A 12-layer LSTM used predicted distances but no residue-pair features

questions.rationale: The authors trained six models at the maximum depth allowed by GPU memory, with three feature sets and two prediction targets.
questions.evidence_quote: In this paper, we use a 12 block ResNet, which is the maximum depth that we could train on the available GPU.

questions.question: What was the effect of adding ESM-1b last-layer attention to a one-hot-only baseline on validation performance?

options.A: F1 reached 0.51, with 0.50 MCC and 0.95 ROC AUC, a 242% F1 gain over one-hot input
options.B: F1 remained 0.15 and MCC fell to zero
options.C: F1 reached 0.22, a 15% gain over SSCpred
options.D: ROC AUC fell from 0.95 to 0.51 after attention was added

questions.rationale: ESM attention supplied substantial pairwise signal compared with sequence identity features alone.
questions.evidence_quote: The attention maps extracted from the last layer of the ESM-1b lead to 0.51, 0.50, 0.56, and 0.95 for F1, MCC, precision and AUC of ROC, respectively. The result is 242% and 178% improvement in the F1-score over models trained on one-hot encoding and SPOT-1D-Single + one-hot encoding, respectively.

questions.question: What did combining all input features add beyond ESM attention from all layers alone?

options.A: It increased F1 by 2.92% and notably improved medium- and long-range precision
options.B: It doubled F1 but reduced all contact precision
options.C: It improved only short-range sensitivity and reduced long-range precision
options.D: It had no effect on validation performance

questions.rationale: The combined representation offered a modest F1 gain with particular benefits for medium- and long-range contacts.
questions.evidence_quote: As expected, concatenating all features together (one-hot encoding + SPOT-1D-Single + ESM-1B attention maps (all layers)) further showed an increase of 2.92% in F1-score over using the attention maps (all layers) only with noticeable improvement in model precision for medium-and long-range contacts, in particular

questions.question: Why were both direct contact classification and distogram prediction retained in the ensemble?

options.A: Direct prediction was slightly better, but the difference was small, so both strategies were used
options.B: Distogram prediction was much better and direct prediction failed
options.C: They produced identical scores by definition and used the same loss
options.D: Direct prediction required MSA, whereas distograms did not

questions.rationale: The small performance gap motivated use of both objective types among the six ensemble members.
questions.evidence_quote: Table 3 and Supplementary Table S3 shows that direct contact-map prediction performs slightly better, but the difference between the two training strategies is small. Thus, both strategies were employed in different models for our final ensemble.

questions.question: How did the ensemble compare with its strongest individual model on the validation set?

options.A: Averaging all six models improved F1 by 4% over the second-best individual model
options.B: It lowered F1 by 4% while improving only ROC AUC
options.C: It matched the best model exactly across all metrics
options.D: It improved accuracy only by adding evolutionary profiles

questions.rationale: The ensemble mean improved across matrices and surpassed every single member in the reported validation comparison.
questions.evidence_quote: The performance of the ensemble (SPOT-Contact-Single) is higher than all individual models, with 4% improvement over the second-best individual model for the F1-score.

questions.question: What input-length limitation did the use of ESM-1b impose on direct SPOT-Contact-Single predictions?

options.A: It could not directly predict contact maps for proteins longer than 1,024 amino acids
options.B: It could not predict proteins shorter than 1,024 amino acids
options.C: It supported only proteins with exactly 1,024 residues
options.D: It limited predictions to proteins with at least 2,048 amino acids

questions.rationale: The authors attribute the upper length limit to the ESM-1b attention-map input.
questions.evidence_quote: Using ESM-1b attention map in SPOT-Contact-Single makes it not possible to directly predict contact maps for proteins with more than 1024 amino acids.
